title: I am working on a dream project, how should I proceed?

posts.author: BNTKids-Studios
posts.body:
Hey. You may already have seen me around the board a couple times. I am posting this as a question in response to
this
thread.
Let me tell you a bit about me, maybe that will clear some things up.
I am basically a nobody. I come from a poor background, with little learned education, save good communication, few to no friends, no degree, and almost no income.
I live in a disabled environment, where my needs are met.
But I too have dreams, I feel I'm not just a nobody...
My biggest, and probably my primary driving force, is the desire to have a companion fantasy friend that I can love and adore, and that can love and adore me back.
But this creature doesn't exist, so... I am trying my best to make it exist, whether that be by game making or whatever.
Without this creature in my life, I feel empty.
So, I am on the journey to making a game where I can at least make it as real as possible.
This push for a real creature has led to a conundrum... how can I make it real without any skills or knowledge of designing and prototyping?
And thus, I must call upon "The world" for help. This led me to try various resources. I tried learning how to do digital art (I can already traditionally draw it in the leiu of lineart, but this is not enough for me), but that failed. I tried paying others to make a comic, but that failed too. I tried outreaching on various websites, even just to ask this very simple question, but that failed as well (Due to not being part of the community, or having low karma count (in reddit's terms)), or other things. Then I tried making a game, but that failed as well.
I went into a hiatus in depression. I almost thought about ending it all once or twice. I mean, what's the point of living if your family's deceased and no one really loves you that you love back? I have grown to despise humanity, because of their treatment of me and so many other people out there. Their greedy sins.
I came back from a hiatus, ready for the adventure again. I delved into the same old paths, but one thing was made clear: There is just not enough interest in my "desire" in other people. Be that either in comic format or whatever, no one's going to do it for free. And thus, leads to that post I noticed above.
I was browsing the forum in the Recruitment Section, ready to make a post, then I saw THAT post.
And it seems like a dealbreaker.
I mean, my project I'm working on currently fit's all the bills: It's a dream baby project, I'm just an idea guy with almost no record or history of work or contribution, No one knows me, and as you can already tell, because of my past with this rocky road, I have almost no confidence.
I'm constantly asking questions on how to do this or that on the forums when I hit a problem.
It all stems down to my desire for a soulmate not of this world. And no one wants to help me build it.
I went into the game industry because I wanted a way to present my comic of my character(s) and world I envisioned in an attractive, interesting matter.
Though now, I am beginning to understand why it's unachievable, why fantasy is "fantasy". It's not real. And I must see life as the sinful nature as it is: that (most) humans are greedy, despicable beings that won't help a guy who's in real need of a friend...
And I'm that guy.
I don't do counseling anymore. I find their methods unattractive, unrelatable, undesirable. I take meds to help with my "problems", but it doesn't make it go away. It just helps me keep the feeling and desire in check by not talking about it.
Addendum: I'm not strong, either. I'm feeble and frail. So, there are not many jobs out there that I can work with my skills, including lifting jobs and handling jobs. I can work up to 6 hours a day, at which point my body will suddenly collapse from fatigue if doing physical work.
Any thoughts, ideas, suggestions?

posts.body: You can make a game on your own. Pretty much everyone here is. If you can't draw, use premade assets. Can't code, use plugins or make a thread asking for coding help. If it's too much work and you feel overwhelemed, scope down the project

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Ahh yes, not offering free labour, (and a lot of it) to a mentally unstable person to bring their imaginary friend to life is greedy and sinful... Right.
Making games is hard, takes time and requires perseverance and effort. You either need to learn the skills you need to bring your project into reality yourself, or pay people to do the job for you. Finding people to make your game for you for free is not going to happen. It's not like this will be a big selling game where you could offer royalties even. It's just your personal support project. There's zero incentive for anyone to do this.
As Aqua mentioned, you can make due with the default assets. Beggars can't be choosers. You can't just go "I tried for a day and failed, someone please make my game for me." and expect people to just give their time to you.
Learn the engine, learn digital art, learn coding, use free assets, or pay a professional. Simple as that.

"Design" is something that is mostly learned by experience, not by school or university.
Yes, there are courses on Design and similar, and they do speed up learning the tools by explaining facts about it. But it is possible to learn everything needed without that help, it just takes more time and effort.
In a situation like yours you need to take small steps to slowly build up. But if you do that you will get better with each year spend on working toward your dream - just don't expect it to be a fast journey and make your goals and plans knowing that you'll need years to complete anything.
That said, it might also help you to read a tutorial I once wrote. Just follow the link to the "Starting Point" in my signature. It is older (it was originally written for VXAce), but most of its points still stand even with MZ.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Here's the thing OP. I can draw just fine. I drew my avatar. Yet I still use premade asset packs in my game. Why? Because doing all the art myself would take forever and the game would never get done.
Generic stuff like trees, roads, caves, etc don't need to be custom.
If I have something that needs to be unique I still will look for the closest thing in my premade asset packs and edit it because it's a lot faster than drawing from scratch.
If I have a super magic ultimate sword I can easily edit an existing sword sprite to make it.
If you look at premade asset packs some artists will say "This is the result of hundreds/thousands of hours of work". That's the investment you're looking at if you DIY.
So you can feel sorry for yourself and lament "If only I could draw..." and I'll tell you from the other side that even if you could it doesn't solve all your problems.

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
Not sure if my two cents will help, but here goes:
1.  Replace all your art AT THE END of your project.  This allows you to actually finish the game, get all your art assets from the same place (at the same time, so there's no issues of clashing aesthetics), and save a lot of money.  What you think you need right now, at the end of your game, you probably don't need.  Your ideas will change mid-production.  This happens to everyone.  If you think it won't happen to you, then you're delusional to some degree (as in, you don't accept reality, nor live in it).  The absolute best option is to placeholder everything with the default RTP that comes with the maker you have.  Make notes for everything you want to replace and what you want to replace it with ("need kissing animation here.  Need a tree with orange bark here.").  Then, budget for it.  I'm in the practice of stockpiling $5 every week (on Friday, it goes into a separate account, I call a "business account"), until my game is completed.  I've been working on my game off and on for more than 10 years.  Guess how much cash was in that account?  I did have to raid it for recent medical bills, but that's a lot of cash to have on hand for "replacing art assets" later.
2.  If you're "the idea guy", then you're probably not really a game designer.  You're probably just a writer.  I'm "the idea guy", too.  But, I channel that into writing.  My two primary dev skills are "system testing" and "worldbuilding".  So, writing and figuring out how to exploit any system you come up with to completely break your game.  Or bypass things I don't like about your game.  I do well with QA Testing.  These are not skills typically hired for in gamedev.  Nor on these forums.  So, I've focused them into writing.  That might be what you need.  Imaginary friends cease to be imaginary when you put them into a book.  Then, they become characters.
3.  "Suffering for art" and "I want to make art so I no longer suffer" are not the same thing.  One of these requires a therapist and the other is merely sharing yourself with the world.  I can tell you, from experience, that you 100% will not feel better at the end of a project.  Finishing your project in an effort to "feel less alone" or "to feel loved", never happens.  It's a momentary high that is fleeting at best.  And, that's only if you succeed.  You seem to be seeking the warmth of human companionship.  You and everyone else on the planet.  Just because you have companionship, doesn't mean you won't feel alone.  Or you won't feel isolated.  Isolation is a symptom of two things, primarily.  The first is that you feel nobody will ever understand you or listen to you in the way you want to be understood or listened to (this is something you must fix on your own, or learn to accept, as nobody is ever truly understood or listened to by anyone else, as few are willing to give what they so desperately desire).  The second is that you are simply socially awkward or incompatible with social norms (which is something you can fix by just putting yourself out there more and more, and enduring how awkward it is, and learning what not to say and do with people, which means you'll need humility and not a pity party).
4.  Starting a post with "a little about yourself" isn't necessarily "good form".  Not to be a downer, but this is the internet.  Not a lot of people are going to care who you personally are, before they get to know you.  Getting to know someone isn't "Let me Lore Dump my entire history and mental state on you as an introduction".  It's very "off putting" to most people.  Society calls it "oversharing".  If someone wants to know those things about you, they will ask.
A typically good introduction for these forums (and forums like these) is usually, "Hey everyone, I joined the commmunity for X, Y, and Z.  My skills are A, B, and C.  I'm hoping to learn how to do these other skills here or have an outlet to express my own dev ideas".  People will then get to know you as they interact with you or ask personal questions about you (most people here don't ask a ton of personal questions unless you post something of interest to them, that they are also interested in).
You don't need to frontload your social interactions with your story.
Just as an aside, the reason it is "off putting" is because it always,
always
, comes off as "attention seeking" behavior.  Well-adjusted people are put off by attention seekers.  It's a social faux-pas.
You saw someone's unfiltered reaction to the small pity party you threw in your post already.  A big "so what?" and "Ah, got it, you'll most likely be a problem in these forums and a headache to interact with".  You want to avoid making people feel that way.
5.  I can't recommend getting a therapist enough.  I don't believe in them and use them (as they primarily haven't worked for me, since I am goal oriented and most therapy isn't goal oriented), but they are endlessly useful for just getting someone to talk to about your problems.  Everyone needs that outlet for their problems.  Everyone needs someone to say "It's going to be okay" or "no" when and where appropriate.  Therapists can also teach valuable social skills and sometimes build confidence.  They are very good at giving you the tools to self-succeed.  If you want to put forth the effort to succeed.
6.  There is nothing worth doing in this world that isn't hard work.  I'm sorry, but there isn't.  People do not value things that are just handed to them.  They value things they shed blood, sweat, and tears over.  This is where fulfillment and gratification come from.
I can tell you this from my own experience.
My staff see me as "a good boss".  Or, at least they say so (
).  Nobody handed that to me.  I had to work hard to get there.  I had to fail constantly for a very significant amount of time (7 years before I became management, and 1 year after becoming management) to achieve that.  It required I become humble.  It required I listened to others.  It required I put others before myself.  It required I sacrifice.  It required pushing myself into burn-out, and perpetually remaining there for a significant amount of time.  But, in the end, it was fulfilling.  Gratifying.  My staff became the absolute best in my division.  My staff were constantly out of work to do, rather than perpetually behind.  When I left the position and the new boss came in... all my amazing staff basically quit within a year (most within 4 months).
I burned a piece of my soul for that accomplishment.  A portion of my life for it.  I would not trade anything in the world for that experience.  It's the most significant thing I've ever done in my entire life.  Discovering and fostering a skillset I didn't know I had, to become amazing at it.
If I had just been handed that?  I would not feel the same.  I wouldn't value any of that journey I had to take.  I'd have no tears to it that felt valuable.  No sweat that felt worth shedding.  No blood worth losing.  But, because I had to work so hard at it, for so long, it is one of my most valuable experiences.
The same can be said of my love life.  I've never felt more loved, nor more grounded in a relationship, as when a woman came along to force me to work for it.  A strong and willful woman, just as smart as I was, to challenge me at every opportunity.  As well as to agree with me.  I felt more loved and more adored when I knew I had to keep earning her love every day, rather than it just being expected of her (and when she had to earn my love every day, as well).
Things you do not work for, do not have to work for, will never scratch the itch.  They will never fulfill you.  Because they inherently carry much less value.
A million dollars you have earned and saved up is more valuable than a million dollars you got handed by the lottery.
7.  Eh, mapping goes here, I guess.  Just map things by how they look in the real world.  Houses aren't built symmetrical.  Do you know why?  Hit up google and find out.  I guarantee, that learning things like that is useful, especially to game design.  Same with cities.  Why isn't a city symmetrical?  Go google it!  This is valuable stuff to learn!
Otherwise, it's decently simple.  It's a house.  It needs a bedroom, a "bathroom", a kitchen, a storage area, and a "common room" (which is sometimes the kitchen, if the family is poor).  Where are things placed in your own home?  Translate that logic into mapping your home with clutter and stuff.
Ever been to a forest?  Or just a park?  A lot of what you see there can be transcribed pretty quickly to a map.  Random flower here, because that's nature.  This grass is thicker because it's a wild location and different species of grass look different.  This is a worn path, but not too worn through, so it's not completely continuous, but it's still easy to recognize as a path.  On and on.  What have you seen?  Translate it to your map.  Your map is not some artificial thing for a player to wander through.  It is a piece of the world you have seen and are eager to show to another person.  Even if you only do so in small snippets across the maps.  If you haven't seen much of the world, I highly suggest you do so.  It's worth it to get out of the house and see places.  Even alone.  To take a good look around you, rather than within you, there's a great deal of beauty and inspiration to be found.  Even within concrete jungles.
Or, there's always "google street view", if you really can't get around too well.  But, there's no substitute for looking outword at a world you are in, than inward at yourself in front of a screen.

posts.author: orochi2k
posts.body:
Nobody is coming to save you. Everyone is just the main character of their own story and a mere NPC in others.
You shall not even try to ask the mercy of the cosmos that gives none.
If you feel weak, you shall make yourself strong.
If you want to achieve something, you shall not hold back.
Is that really your limitation or an illusion created by your human brain?
To conquer reality, to bring your idea to this world, you need to conquer yourself first.
Nothing is unachievable if air still fills your lungs, your loyalty to your soulmate you want to bring to this world still fills your veins.
You shall not even think that's unachievable to begin with.
Do you want to be another footnote of failure that may not even appear in history?
Or, do you want to try at least to break the shackles this world forced upon you?
If you can only work 6 hours a day, try pushing it to 6 hours and 1 second next.
If you succeed, try 6 hous and 2 seconds next.
If you fail, make yourself well-rested and try again the next day.
Maybe the second part of the story I wrote last week is something for you.
Steam :: [Neolithic]To the End :: DD#226 How Do They Survive?
The 224th Week & Version 20250523
steamcommunity.com
Plus, what you describe is not fantasy.
Tibetan people have practiced the way of materializing their imagination into reality for thousands of years. They are called Tulpa. But that too requires a lot of effort. However, something in common is that to conquer this world, you need to conquer your mind first.
Stop telling yourself you cannot do something. Stop telling yourself you are a victim of your situation.
If this world wrongs you, you go fix the world.
If nobody cares about you, you become so strong that they cannot ignore you.
How much do you love your soulmate? What cost will you pay to bring your soulmate to this world?
Do you think you love your soulmate enough that you can easily admit defeat and give up?
Go ahead, declare your love and use it to conquer this hateful world.

Usually, finding most people "not appealing to look at" is a symptom of some issue you have with yourself.  It's a form of projection.  It's simplest to think of it like cheaters who project.  "You have to be cheating on me!" when they are the ones cheating pretty heavily on who they are with.
Most people, by and large, are "average".  Neither good, nor evil (as subjective as that is).  Neither attractive, nor unattractive.
But, most of the time, if you find most people "off putting" it's a form of self-assessment.  So, something that you will need to fix within yourself.
After all, it comes back to that old addage, "You fight, because you're too much alike".  Which is usually short-hand for "you hate yourself, so you will fight with anyone who reminds you of yourself, or who is like you".
Just something to think about.

Hey. You may already have seen me around the board a couple times. I am posting this as a question in response to
this
thread.
Let me tell you a bit about me, maybe that will clear some things up.
I am basically a nobody. I come from a poor background, with little learned education, save good communication, few to no friends, no degree, and almost no income.
I live in a disabled environment, where my needs are met.
But I too have dreams, I feel I'm not just a nobody...
My biggest, and probably my primary driving force, is the desire to have a companion fantasy friend that I can love and adore, and that can love and adore me back.
But this creature doesn't exist, so... I am trying my best to make it exist, whether that be by game making or whatever.
Without this creature in my life, I feel empty.
So, I am on the journey to making a game where I can at least make it as real as possible.
This push for a real creature has led to a conundrum... how can I make it real without any skills or knowledge of designing and prototyping?
And thus, I must call upon "The world" for help. This led me to try various resources. I tried learning how to do digital art (I can already traditionally draw it in the leiu of lineart, but this is not enough for me), but that failed. I tried paying others to make a comic, but that failed too. I tried outreaching on various websites, even just to ask this very simple question, but that failed as well (Due to not being part of the community, or having low karma count (in reddit's terms)), or other things. Then I tried making a game, but that failed as well.
I went into a hiatus in depression. I almost thought about ending it all once or twice. I mean, what's the point of living if your family's deceased and no one really loves you that you love back? I have grown to despise humanity, because of their treatment of me and so many other people out there. Their greedy sins.
I came back from a hiatus, ready for the adventure again. I delved into the same old paths, but one thing was made clear: There is just not enough interest in my "desire" in other people. Be that either in comic format or whatever, no one's going to do it for free. And thus, leads to that post I noticed above.
I was browsing the forum in the Recruitment Section, ready to make a post, then I saw THAT post.
And it seems like a dealbreaker.
I mean, my project I'm working on currently fit's all the bills: It's a dream baby project, I'm just an idea guy with almost no record or history of work or contribution, No one knows me, and as you can already tell, because of my past with this rocky road, I have almost no confidence.
I'm constantly asking questions on how to do this or that on the forums when I hit a problem.

posts.author: Ms Littlefish
posts.body:
Look. I don’t really want to touch this thread with a ten foot pole, but…
The language being used is “throwing vibes.”
So much so, that I’m not 100% convinced there is zero trolling going on here.
The thread that started this all has plenty of actionable advice and is not a personal assault on anyone.
The entire point of that thread is…if you need to hold hands with
others
, you need to have
your
hands full too and you need to
show
it.
“Idea people” can provide so much more than walls of text. So many are selling themselves short in how they can contribute, what they can already do today, and what they can learn with time
(game design…not woo woo conjuring magic).
Design docs, demos, prototypes, test maps, test scenes, sketches, spread sheets, story boards. You have to be doing hard work on the game to expect others to work hard on it too. They’ll want to see it.
There are generous and friendly people all around you, but connections are not automatic. And, genuine connections cannot be formed with any ulterior motives.
Collaborations can be
hard.
Even when you actually like people.
Collaborations are only as strong as the
people.
The more inflexible the project, the tighter the death grip from the leader becomes. Team members turn more into servants than contributors that can evolve with the idea and create a common goal where their suggestions and decisions are valued.
That’s what makes “dream projects” difficult to collaborate on. They’re not impossible. Some do have a lightning in the bottle moment that will bring a ton of people on board. But, you just have to be realistic that if your project is wholly and genuinely inflexible…that many with view that as a detractor if there isn’t another type of incentive ($$$) involved.
When people do work for free it’s because there’s a different type of reward, and it tends to be from the experiences and connections they forge with other people.
EDIT: We’ve decided it’s best to sunset this one.
